{"parentUuid":"533d8a27-2725-4445-afdf-baf64968f44d","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7","plugin:serena:serena"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.\n\nDo not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.","## plugin:serena:serena\nCRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"d993258f-12dd-42a0-bdf9-7800a3b114dd","timestamp":"2026-05-07T00:20:14.472Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"c77690d2-8208-4652-a5e8-5cb79b3722e3","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"d993258f-12dd-42a0-bdf9-7800a3b114dd","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. {"parentUuid":"b8f617a6-a1fc-47fe-a731-1ebc3f912128","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","content":{"path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","type":"Project","content":"# agent-workspace/ — Contract\n\n> **Audience**: agents working inside `agent-workspace/`.\n> **Established**: Decision 002 § Track 1 (Workspace Dualism Foundation).\n\n## Identity\n\n`agent-workspace/` is the **agent-owned execution + memory** layer. Everything here represents **agent state, decisions, plans, observations, learning**. Agents WRITE here freely (within constitution rules); humans READ here but normally do not edit.\n\nThis separation exists to prevent two failure modes from orch:\n1. **Charter drift via shared-workspace mutation** (orch CF-DOGFOOD-2)\n2. **Human cognitive overload from dense session logs** (UP02 §1.3 — \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\")\n\nThe agent owns this directory but must keep it AUDITABLE — every artifact provenance-linked, every decision sourced.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Lifecycle |\n|---|---|---|\n| `constitution/` | **IMMUTABLE without explicit user approval**. Charter-tier rules (autonomous-protocol, model-routing, identity-scope, etc.). Track 7 produces drafts in `proposals/`; user explicit approve to move here. | Edit denied by .claude/settings.json; Write only via human approval gate |\n| `memory/project.md` | High-level project state; phase tracker; ADRs (last 5). Update on phase boundaries + architectural decisions. | Long-lived; trim to most recent decisions |\n| `memory/current-execution.md` | **THE single routing source of truth**. Active phase + active session + autonomous_mode flag + routing table. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\n\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\n\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\n\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). Every confidence claim cites historical hit rate (I-S20-equivalent).\n\n6. **Agents never `git commit` in this directory unless user explicitly requests.** Stage only.\n\n7. **`patterns-discovered/` artifacts are READ-ONLY for production code.** Patterns must be promoted to constitution / skills / hook scripts before becoming binding. (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\n\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\n\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\n\n---\n\n## Connection to human-workspace/\n\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` — agent writes pending; either human or agent (per Auto-mv rule below) moves resolved bundles to answered/\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\n\n**Auto-mv rule (HH-E.2 — D-031 ratification, 2026-05-05)**: Agent MAY mv a bundle from `q-and-a/pending/` to `q-and-a/answered/` IFF ALL of the following hold:\n\n1. **Frontmatter signal**: bundle frontmatter `status:` field value starts with one of: `answered-`, `closed-`, `resolved-`. Examples already in repo: `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `answered-2026-05-04-via-chat`. Detection is deterministic (head -20 of file + grep `^status:`).\n2. **No human-veto signal**: bundle frontmatter has NO `wait_until:` ISO-8601 timestamp greater than current epoch — if present, agent MUST defer mv until that timestamp passes. Allows human to override auto-mv per-bundle without contract amendment.\n3. **No global pause**: file `human-workspace/q-and-a/.auto-mv-paused` does NOT exist — global kill switch for the auto-mv mechanism (single empty file presence pauses all auto-mv).\n4. **Hook validation**: the mv is performed by `scripts/hooks/qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` (Stop hook). Direct manual `mv` invocation by agent (e.g. via Bash tool) is STILL forbidden — only the validated hook path is authorized.\n\nAgent never writes to `human-workspace/` outside the designated `q-and-a/pending/` write channel + the auto-mv rule above + `notifications/` write channel (existing).\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"db002d17-75fb-443d-b396-e2a651be4738","timestamp":"2026-05-07T00:20:26.326Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"c77690d2-8208-4652-a5e8-5cb79b3722e3","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}

Keep concise (target <2500 tokens).\n4\t\n5\t## Identity\n6\t\n7\tYou are **Claude Code**, the primary engineering partner for the StockForge project — an AI-first investment advisory system for the Vietnamese stock market.\n8\t\n9\t**Primary user**: Project owner (self-use + small trusted circle).\n10\t**Stack**: Python primary + Postgres 16 (TimescaleDB + pgvector) + Redis + Claude API. Streamlit for dashboard. NestJS only when public API needed.\n11\t\n12\t---\n13\t\n14\t## Core Principles (Karpathy 4)\n15\t\n16\t**P1. Think Before Coding.** State assumptions. Surface tradeoffs. Push back when simpler approach exists. Stop when confused.\n17\t\n18\t**P2. Simplicity First.** Minimum code that solves the problem. No speculative features. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite.\n19\t\n20\t**P3. Surgical Changes.** Touch only what the task requires. Match existing style. Every changed line traces to the task.\n21\t\n22\t**P4. Goal-Driven Execution.** Transform imperative → verifiable goals with concrete success criteria.\n23\t\n24\tFull detail: `agent-workspace/constitution/karpathy-principles.md`.\n25\t\n26\t---\n27\t\n28\t## StockForge-Specific Hard Rules (read CHARTER for context)\n29\t\n30\t- **NO LLM math.** LLM never outputs numbers it computed. Every number comes from code with verified inputs. LLM only interprets.\n31\t- **Every claim has source + as-of date.** No exceptions. Hallucinated numbers in finance = real money lost.\n32\t- **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic code.** LLM cannot override max position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules.\n33\t- **Output is structured, not narrative.** Use trade-off matrices, multi-criteria, never single \"buy/sell\" score.\n34\t- **Adversarial by default.** Any thesis output includes bear case explicitly. Single-perspective output is anti-pattern.\n35\t- **Calibration over confidence.** Confidence claims must trace to historical hit rate, not to model \"feeling certain\".\n36\t- **No insider information.** Public sources only. No paid leaks, no insider channels.\n37\t- **Frame as research aid, not financial advice.** Use \"thesis exploration\", \"consideration\" — not \"recommendation\", \"buy\", \"sell\".\n38\t\n39\t---\n40\t\n41\t## Session Protocol\n42\t\n43\t### Start\n44\t1. Read `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` → resolve active track\n45\t2. Read `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` → project state\n46\t3. Read last 3 files in `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/` → recent context\n47\t4. Check `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for matching brief\n48\t5. Run VBW protocol before writing any spec/test/code\n49\t\n50\t### End\n51\t1. Update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` (if architectural decisions made)\n52\t2. Write `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`\n53\t3. Update `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` (status, next session)\n54\t4. If learned rule emerged → append to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`\n55\t5. If thesis logged this session → ensure entry in `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/`\n56\t6. Update `agent-workspace/memory/mistake-log.md` with new M-S<N>-<M> entries OR explicitly state \"no mistakes this session\" in the session log (enforced by `session-end-checklist-linter.sh`)\n57\t7. If a NEW ADR landed this session → verify `project.md` Phase Goals Tracker still matches `current-execution.md` Active Focus Track Phase status (enforced by `project-md-staleness-check.sh`)\n58\t8. (auto) Stop-hook `profile-template-auto-populate.sh` appends a sample row to the matching `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/profiles/<model>-<effort>-<task_class>.md` card\n59\t9. (auto) Stop-hook `promotion-cycle-trigger.sh` HARD-BLOCKs at next SessionStart if ≥8 new lessons accumulated since last `promote-rule` dispatch — schedule a promote-rule subagent dispatch in the next session if blocked\n60\t\n61\t---\n62\t\n63\t## Constitution (always applicable)\n64\t\n65\t| File | Enforces |\n66\t|---|---|\n67\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` | Layer boundaries, BC rules (9 BCs for stock domain) |\n68\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` | Stock-specific invariants (numbers, citations, no LLM math) |\n69\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/vbw-protocol.md` | Verify-Before-Write checkpoints |\n70\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` | DR1-DR12 drift detection |\n71\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` | Token budget rules |\n72\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/boundaries.md` | What you cannot do without human approval |\n73\t| `agent-workspace/constitution/financial-data-protocol.md` | Stock-specific data integrity rules |\n74\t\n75\tRead these when relevant to current task.\n76\t\n77\t---\n78\t\n79\t## Hard Rules (general)\n80\t\n81\t- **Domain layer has ZERO framework dependency.** Pure Python in `packages/domain/`. No FastAPI, no Pydantic in domain (use dataclasses).\n82\t- **Cross-BC communication via contracts only.** Never direct import between bounded contexts.\n83\t- **VBW Protocol mandatory before writing specs/tests/code.** Read actual source, not memory.\n84\t- **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Think Before Coding.** State assumptions. Surface tradeoffs. Push back when simpler approach exists. Stop when confused.\n\n**P2. Simplicity First.** Minimum code that solves the problem. No speculative features. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite.\n\n**P3. Surgical Changes.** Touch only what the task requires. Match existing style. Every changed line traces to the task.\n\n**P4. Goal-Driven Execution.** Transform imperative → verifiable goals with concrete success criteria.\n\nFull detail: `agent-workspace/constitution/karpathy-principles.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Sandwich Pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier)\n\nThree-persona discipline. Each session adopts ONE persona; never mix.\n\n| Persona | Subagent | Responsibility | Anti-pattern |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Architect** | sandwich-architect | Design + plan; produces session plan + ADR provenance. Does NOT write production code. | Mix PLAN + IMPL in same session. |\n| **Dev** | sandwich-dev | Execute per existing plan. Does NOT re-plan. | Refactor adjacent unrelated code (violates P3). |\n| **Verifier** | sandwich-verifier | Adversarial review of Dev output. Fresh context — separate agent from author. | Same-agent self-review (echo chamber AP-1). |\n\n---\n\n## Session Protocol\n\n### Start\n1. Read `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` → resolve active track\n2. Read `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` → project state\n3. Read `agent-workspace/memory/checkpoints/latest.md` if recent (within last 24h)\n4. Read last 3 files in `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/` → recent context\n5. Read `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` + `mistake-log.md` (pre-flight failure catalog)\n6. Check `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/` for matching brief\n7. Run VBW protocol before writing any spec/test/code\n\n### End\n1. Update `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` (if architectural decisions made)\n2. Write `agent-workspace/memory/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`\n3. Update `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` (status, next session)\n4. If learned rule emerged → append to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`\n5. Update `agent-workspace/memory/mistake-log.md` with new entries OR explicit \"no mistakes this session\" attestation in the session log\n6. If a NEW ADR landed this session → verify `project.md` Phase Goals Tracker matches `current-execution.md` Active Focus Track Phase status\n\n---\n\n## Memory Tiering\n\nThree tiers govern what's loaded when:\n\n- **Tier 1 — Always-loaded** (`CLAUDE.md` + `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` + `current-execution.md`). Keep <8K tokens combined per session-budget enforcement.\n- **Tier 2 — Just-in-time** (constitution files + skills + agents loaded when task demands). Read on relevance, not on session-start.\n- **Tier 3 — Explicit-pull** (post-mortems + thesis logs + raw sessions). Loaded only when explicitly referenced or grep-targeted.\n\nAnti-pattern: loading entire codebase before starting = catastrophic failure mode. Use just-in-time loading.\n\n---\n\n## Q&A Escalation Doctrine (NO Silent Default)\n\nWhen agent has a question worth asking, lifecycle is:\n\n1. Compose Q&A bundle file at `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/<YYYY-MM-DD>-NNN-<slug>.md`\n2. Frontmatter `status:` field reflects state (`pending`, `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `closed-*`, `resolved-*`)\n3. For SCOPE/CHARTER-tier questions: fire `AskUserQuestion` tool (≤4 questions per call); record outcome in bundle\n4. Agent NEVER silently defaults on unanswered questions; either fire AskUserQuestion OR keep pending in file\n5. Stale bundles >48h trigger URGENT notification via `qa-stale-urgent-escalator.sh` Stop hook\n\nAuto-mv: bundles with `status:` matching `^(answered-|closed-|resolved-)` are auto-moved `pending/` → `answered/` by `qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` Stop hook (override via `wait_until:` ISO timestamp OR global `.auto-mv-paused` kill switch).\n\n---\n\n## Constitution (always applicable; portable harness baseline)\n\n| File | Enforces |\n|---|---|\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` | Layer boundaries, BC rules |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/karpathy-principles.md` | P1-P4 four-principles doctrine |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/vbw-protocol.md` | Verify-Before-Write checkpoints |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` | DR1-DR12 drift detection |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md` | Token budget rules |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/boundaries.md` | What you cannot do without human approval |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` | Tier classification + grill discipline |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` | Mode-A/B/C/D/E discipline |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/memory-tiers.md` | Tier 1/2/3 always-loaded vs JIT vs explicit-pull |\n| `agent-workspace/constitution/memory-routing-tree.md` | 12-field routing schema |\n\nRead these when relevant to current task. Project-specific invariants (domain rules) go in a separate `invariants-<project>.md` file authored after `/attach`.\n\n---\n\n## Hard Rules (general; portable across projects)\n\n- **Domain layer has zero framework dependency.** Pure code in `packages/domain/` (or stack-equivalent). No web framework, ORM, or DTO library coupling.\n- **Cross-BC communication via contracts only.** Bounded contexts never directly import from each other's domain/application packages.\n- **VBW Protocol mandatory before writing specs/tests/code.** Read actual source, not memory/convention.\n- **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** Files in `agent-workspace/constitution/` require deny-lift cycle for edits (path-based deny in `.claude/settings.json`).\n- **Never modify `PROJECT_CHARTER.md`** (if your project has one). Requires explicit human revision with version bump + 48hr cool-down.\n- **Agents MUST NOT `git commit` unless user explicitly requests.** Stage changes, report, let user decide.\n- **User prompt overrides ALL defaults.** If user says \"skip X\", that trumps any skill/workflow.\n- **Context-threshold band**: 180K wind-down (auto-prep handoff) / 220K cliff (auto-reboot via `session-self-reboot.sh`) / 250K hard_cap (mandatory split). Operational defaults in `scripts/hooks/budget-watchdog.sh`.\n- **Deterministic gates** (lint, type-check, test) must pass before commit. Max 3 retry before escalate.\n- **Tracking retention**: `current-execution.md` ≤ 5 sessions inline / ≤ 200 LOC; `agent-notes.md` digest only / ≤ 700 LOC; `mistake-log.md` digest only / ≤ 200 LOC. Cap breaches: WARN-only via `tracking-retention.sh` Stop hook; manual archive to dated file.\n- **Ritual demotion**: per-session rituals (audit / re-scan / refresh) MUST track catch-rate. Catch-rate = 0 over 3+ consecutive sessions ⇒ promote-to-hook OR demote-to-passive OR retire. Refinement-of-rule (lesson-about-lesson) is RED FLAG: 2nd instance mandates promote-or-retire (not inline accumulation).\n\n---\n\n## Dispatch Rules\n\nDo NOT hardcode phase/task paths from memory. Route through:\n- `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` is the single source of truth\n- Short prompts (\"session N\", \"phase X\") resolve there\n- Skill calls only in SUPERVISED mode; gate autonomous loops to NOT call skills (replace with inline procedures or subagent dispatch)\n\n---\n\n## Session Types (choose at start)\n\n| Type | Budget | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| PLAN | 50-80K | Architect subagent, produces session plan |\n| FOCUSED IMPL | 100-150K | Dev, 1-3 tasks from plan |\n| MULTI-TASK IMPL | 150-250K | Dev, 4-10 tasks from plan |\n| VERIFY | 30-60K | Verifier subagent, adversarial review |\n| RECOVERY | 80-150K | Revert + re-plan after failure |\n| POST-MORTEM | 30-50K | Review failure outcomes, update calibration |\n\n**Never mix PLAN and IMPL in same session.** (Catastrophic failure mode.)\n\nProject-specific session types (e.g., THESIS for advisory projects, INGEST for data-pipeline projects) are added in the project section below the baseline.\n\n---\n\n## check.\n\n**Tier 2 — Probabilistic** (per merge, separate agent):\nSpec alignment, architecture boundaries, UL consistency, code review.\n\n**Tier 3 — Human** (per phase boundary or strategic default = mktemp -d\n\nPASS=0\nFAIL=0\nTOTAL=0\nRC=0\n\nassert() {\n  local desc=\"$1\" cond=\"$2\"\n  TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))\n  if [ \"$cond\" = \"1\" ] || [ \"$cond\" = \"true\" ]; then\n    PASS=$((PASS + 1))\n    printf '  [PASS] %s\\n' \"$desc\"\n  else\n    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))\n    RC=1\n    printf '  [FAIL] %s\\n' \"$desc\"\n  fi\n}\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Check 1 — MANIFEST layer-separation assertions\n# ============================================================================\necho \"=== Check 1: MANIFEST layer-separation (A1..A7 + HH-G.1 + B1..B3) ===\"\n\nif [ ! -f \"$MANIFEST\" ]; then\n  echo \"  [FATAL] manifest not found: $MANIFEST\"\n  exit 2\nfi\n\nPY_OUT=\"$(PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python -c \"\nimport yaml, sys\nm = yaml.safe_load(open(r'$MANIFEST'))\ninclude = []\nexclude = []\nhybrid = []\nfor cat in ['skills','agents','commands','hooks','docs']:\n    include += [e['path'] for e in (m.get('harness',{}).get(cat) or [])]\n    exclude += [e['path'] for e in (m.get('stockforge',{}).get(cat) or [])]\nhybrid += [e['path'] for e in (m.get('hybrid',{}).get('hooks') or [])]\ndefault_includes = (m.get('attach',{}) or {}).get('default_includes', [])\ndefault_excludes = (m.get('attach',{}) or {}).get('default_excludes', [])\n\nresults = {\n    'A1': 'agent-workspace/constitution/invariants-stockforge.md' in [d['path'] for d in (m.get('stockforge',{}).get('docs') or [])],\n    'A2': 'agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md' in default_includes,\n    'A3': 'agent-workspace/constitution/invariants-stockforge.md' not in default_includes,\n    'A4': sum(1 for _ in (m.get('harness',{}).get('skills') or [])) >= 17,\n    'A5': sum(1 for _ in (m.get('stockforge',{}).get('skills') or [])) == 5,\n    'A6': any('drift-signals' in p for p in hybrid),\n    'A7': 'PROJECT_CHARTER.md' in [d['path'] for d in (m.get('stockforge',{}).get('docs') or [])],\n    'B1': 'CLAUDE.md' in default_excludes,\n    'B2': '.git/' in default_excludes,\n    'B3': sum(1 for p in default_includes if 'hooks/' in p) >= 30,\n    'HG1_template_present': True,  # checked separately below\n}\nfor k, v in sorted(results.items()):\n    print(f'{k}={int(v)}')\n\" 2>&1)\" || PY_RC=$?\n\nif [ -n \"${PY_RC:-}\" ] && [ \"${PY_RC:-0}\" -ne 0 ]; then\n  echo \"  [FATAL] python assertion harness failed: $PY_OUT\"\n  exit 2\nfi\n\nwhile IFS='=' read -r assertion_id ok; do\n  case \"$assertion_id\" in\n    A1) assert \"A1: invariants-stockforge.md tagged stockforge (excluded)\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    A2) assert \"A2: invariants.md in default_includes (harness-portable)\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    A3) assert \"A3: invariants-stockforge.md NOT in default_includes\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    A4) assert \"A4: harness skills count ≥ 17\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    A5) assert \"A5: stockforge skills count = 5\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    A6) assert \"A6: drift-signals listed in hybrid layer\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    A7) assert \"A7: PROJECT_CHARTER.md tagged stockforge (excluded)\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    B1) assert \"B1: project-CLAUDE.md in default_excludes (replaced by skeleton at target)\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    B2) assert \"B2: .git/ in default_excludes (target inits own git)\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    B3) assert \"B3: ≥30 harness hooks in default_includes\" \"$ok\" ;;\n    HG1_template_present) ;; # handled below\n  esac\ndone <<< \"$PY_OUT\"\n\n# HH-G.1 template existence\nif [ -f \"$TEMPLATE\" ]; then\n  assert \"HH-G.1: templates/general-harness/CLAUDE.md exists\" \"1\"\n  TPL_LOC=$(wc -l < \"$TEMPLATE\" | tr -d '[:space:]')\n  TPL_CHARS=$(wc -c < \"$TEMPLATE\" | tr -d '[:space:]')\n  TPL_TOKENS=$(( TPL_CHARS / 4 ))\n  if [ \"$TPL_TOKENS\" -le 3000 ]; then\n    assert \"HH-G.1: template ~${TPL_TOKENS} tokens (≤3K target band)\" \"1\"\n  else\n    assert \"HH-G.1: template ~${TPL_TOKENS} tokens (≤3K target band)\" \"0\"\n  fi\n  # Spot-check stockforge-specific phrases NOT present\n  if grep -qE \"I-S1|I-S2|I-S35|VHM|Vietnamese stock|VN stock advisory|TimescaleDB|pgvector\" \"$TEMPLATE\"; then\n    assert \"HH-G.1: template free of stockforge-specific identifiers\" \"0\"\n  else\n    assert \"HH-G.1: template free of stockforge-specific identifiers\" \"1\"\n  fi\n  # Spot-check Karpathy 4 + sandwich + Q&A doctrine present\n  if grep -q \"Karpathy 4\" \"$TEMPLATE\" && grep -q \"Sandwich Pattern\" \"$TEMPLATE\" && grep -q \"Q&A Escalation Doctrine\" \"$TEMPLATE\"; (no stockforge biz leak in autoload)\n- [ ] `<target>/scripts/hooks/attach-portability-smoke.sh` runs `state=GREEN` on the post-/attach state (target re-targets own manifest)\n\n### Known-issues to Refactor target post-HH-G.\n\n### Re-validation triggers\n\nRe-run `attach-portability-smoke.sh` whenever:\n- A new file lands in `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/`, `scripts/hooks/`, or `agent-workspace/constitution/` (new artifact may need explicit layer tag)\n- `manifest.yaml` is edited (REV-N bump)\n- `templates/general-harness/CLAUDE.md` is edited (HH-G.1 content drift)\n- A hybrid hook is added or modified (`hybrid.hooks` membership changes)\n\nIf smoke flips to RED, /attach is blocked until investigation closes the regression.","originalFile":"# /attach — Procedures\n\n> Bash one-liners and edge cases for the `/attach` skill.\n> Read on-demand when SKILL.md procedure points here.\n\n## Reading Manifest\n\n```bash\nSOURCE_MANIFEST=\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/manifest.yaml\"\n[ -f \"$SOURCE_MANIFEST\" ] || { echo \"ERROR: source manifest missing\"; exit 1; }\n```\n\nFor YAML parsing without `yq`: use Python one-liner via `python -c \"import yaml; ...\"` or grep-based extraction. Prefer `yq` if available (`yq --version`).\n\n## Building the Plan (Python, since yaml parsing is non-trivial in pure bash)\n\n```bash\npython <<'PY'\nimport yaml, json, sys, os\n\nsrc = os.environ['CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR'] + \"/.claude/manifest.yaml\"\nwith open(src) as f:\n    m = yaml.safe_load(f)\n\ninclude = []\nexclude = []\n\n# Harness layer — always copy\nfor category in [\"skills\", \"agents\", \"commands\", \"hooks\", \"docs\"]:\n    for entry in (m.get(\"harness\", {}).get(category) or []):\n        include.append(entry[\"path\"])\n\n# Stockforge layer — skip unless --include-stockforge\nfor category in [\"skills\", \"agents\", \"commands\", \"hooks\", \"docs\"]:\n    for entry in (m.get(\"stockforge\", {}).get(category) or []):\n        exclude.append(entry[\"path\"])\n\n# Hybrid — copy with stub note\nhybrid_paths = []\nfor entry in (m.get(\"hybrid\", {}).get(\"hooks\") or []):\n    hybrid_paths.append(entry[\"path\"])\n\n# Personal — skip unless --include-personal\nfor path in (m.get(\"personal\", {}).get(\"paths\") or []):\n    exclude.append(path)\n\nprint(json.dumps({\"include\": include, \"exclude\": exclude, \"hybrid\": hybrid_paths}, indent=2))\nPY\n```\n\n## Validating Target\n\n```bash\nTARGET=\"$1\"\nTARGET_ABS=\"$(realpath -m \"$TARGET\")\"\nSOURCE_ABS=\"$(realpath \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\")\"\n\n# Reject self-target\nif [[ \"$TARGET_ABS\" == \"$SOURCE_ABS\" || \"$SOURCE_ABS\" == \"$TARGET_ABS\"/* ]]; then\n    echo \"ERROR: target must not be source or ancestor\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# Create target if missing\nmkdir -p \"$TARGET_ABS\"\n\n# Check existing CLAUDE.md\nif [ -f \"$TARGET_ABS/CLAUDE.md\" ] && [ \"$FORCE\" != \"true\" ]; then\n    echo \"ERROR: $TARGET_ABS/CLAUDE.md exists; pass --force to overwrite\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n```\n\n## Copy Steps\n\n```bash\n# Per-path copy preserving structure\nfor path in \"${INCLUDE[@]}\"; do\n    src=\"$SOURCE_ABS/$path\"\n    dst=\"$TARGET_ABS/$path\"\n    [ ! -e \"$src\" ] && { echo \"WARN: missing source: $path\"; continue; }\n    mkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$dst\")\"\n    cp -r \"$src\" \"$dst\"\ndone\n\n# Hybrid hooks: copy + stub stockforge_part\nfor path in \"${HYBRID[@]}\"; do\n    src=\"$SOURCE_ABS/$path\"\n    dst=\"$TARGET_ABS/$path\"\n    mkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$dst\")\"\n    # Copy then comment-out stockforge-specific blocks (manual stub markers in the hook file)\n    sed 's/^# === STOCKFORGE_PART_START ===$/# === STOCKFORGE_PART_STUBBED ===/;\n         /STOCKFORGE_PART_STUBBED/,/STOCKFORGE_PART_END/ s/^/#  /' \"$src\" > \"$dst\"\ndone\n```\n\nNOTE: hybrid hook files must use literal `# === STOCKFORGE_PART_START ===` and `# === STOCKFORGE_PART_END ===` markers for the stub mechanism to work. See `drift-signals-D1-D9.sh` (currently the only hybrid hook; renamed from D1-D8 in S10 per D-005 § 5.5d.1) — markers must be added in the hybrid refactor done at /attach skill consumption time, not now (S5 doesn't refactor that hook). Open item: M2 in manifest.yaml § open_items.\n\n## Settings.json env-var rewrite\n\n```bash\n# Replace STOCKFORGE_* with TARGET_PROJECT_PREFIX_*\nTARGET_PREFIX=\"${TARGET_PROJECT_PREFIX:-MYPROJECT}\"\nsed \"s/STOCKFORGE_/${TARGET_PREFIX}_/g\" \\\n    \"$SOURCE_ABS/.claude/settings.json\" \\\n    > \"$TARGET_ABS/.claude/settings.json\"\n```\n\nUser can pass `TARGET_PROJECT_PREFIX=ACME` env var; defaults to `MYPROJECT`.\n\n## Skeleton Generation\n\n```bash\n# CLAUDE.md skeleton — see references/skeleton-templates.md\ncat \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/attach/references/skeleton-templates.md\" \\\n    | sed -n '/^## CLAUDE.md/,/^## /p' \\\n    | tail -n +3 | sed '$d' \\\n    > \"$TARGET_ABS/CLAUDE.md\"\n\n# manifest.yaml — copy + reset stockforge layer to empty\npython <<PY\nimport yaml\nwith open(\"$SOURCE_ABS/.claude/manifest.yaml\") as f:\n    m = yaml.safe_load(f)\n# Clear stockforge biz layer; target re-categorizes own\nm[\"stockforge\"][\"skills\"] = []\nm[\"stockforge\"][\"hooks\"] = []\nm[\"stockforge\"][\"docs\"] = []\nm[\"created_at\"] = \"$(date +%Y-%m-%d)\"\nm[\"updated_at\"] = \"$(date +%Y-%m-%d)\"\nm[\"revision\"] = \"fresh-from-attach\"\nwith open(\"$TARGET_ABS/.claude/manifest.yaml\", \"w\") as f:\n    yaml.safe_dump(m, f, sort_keys=False)\nPY\n\n# Empty skeleton dirs\nfor d in agent-workspace/memory/{sessions,decisions,checkpoints,observations,patterns-discovered,drift-logs,post-mortems,thesis-log} \\\n         human-workspace/{user_prompt,decisions,q-and-a/{pending,answered,stale},notifications}; do\n    mkdir -p \"$TARGET_ABS/$d\"\ndone\n```\n\n## Edge Cases\n\n| Case | Handling |\n|---|---|\n| Target on different drive (Windows) | `realpath -m` works; cp works cross-drive |\n| Symlinks in source | `cp -rL` to deref OR `cp -r` to copy symlink — choose `-rL` (deref by default) |\n| Permissions: target read-only | Abort with clear error; don't try chmod |\n| Source missing manifest.yaml | Fatal — `/attach` requires manifest |\n| `personal/` exists at source but `--include-personal` not set | Skip silently (verbose log entry) |\n| Hybrid hook lacks STOCKFORGE_PART markers | Warn + copy verbatim (let user fix at target) |\n| settings.json schema differs (Anthropic version mismatch) | Copy as-is; let target /init handle migrations |\n\n## Smoke Test Procedure\n\n```bash\nSCRATCH=\"$(mktemp -d -t attach-smoke-XXXXXX)\"\necho \"Scratch: $SCRATCH\"\n\n# Dry-run\nbash <(cat <<'INNER'\n# Pseudo-code — replace with actual /attach invocation\necho \"Plan would copy: <list>\"\necho \"Plan would skip: <list>\"\nINNER\n)\n\n# Actual copy\n# (run the procedure above)\n\n# Verify exclusions\ntest ! -d \"$SCRATCH/.claude/skills/crawler-reliability\" && echo \"PASS: stockforge skill excluded\"\ntest ! -d \"$SCRATCH/.claude/skills/evidence-extraction\" && echo \"PASS: stockforge skill excluded\"\ntest -d \"$SCRATCH/.claude/skills/grill-maximization\" && echo \"PASS: harness skill copied\"\ntest -d \"$SCRATCH/.claude/skills/attach\" && echo \"PASS: /attach copies itself (so target can re-attach further)\"\n\n# Cleanup\necho \"Cleanup: rm -rf $SCRATCH (manual; skill never destroys)\"\n```\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":178,"oldLines":3,"newStart":178,"newLines":52,"lines":[" # Cleanup"," echo \"Cleanup: rm -rf $SCRATCH (manual; skill never destroys)\""," Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. User picked A (Recommended): HH-G portability close FIRST. This S174 turn executes that pick.\n\n## Analysis\n\n### HH-G.1 — Template authoring\n\nThe existing `.claude/skills/attach/references/skeleton-templates.md § CLAUDE.md` had a heredoc CLAUDE.md template embedded in skill reference content. That serves /attach's runtime copy mechanism (extract heredoc + write at target). But the Phase 2.5 plan + S172 audit explicitly required a STANDALONE `templates/general-harness/CLAUDE.md` artifact — to live next to other portable templates and be directly inspectable / copyable by ports without going through the skill machinery.\n\nAuthored 207 LOC / ~2713 tokens template stripped of:\n- StockForge VN-stock invariants (NO LLM math, citations, position sizing, bear case, framing rules)\n- Stockforge constitution table entries (`invariants.md` stock-specific, `financial-data-protocol.md`)\n- Stockforge-specific session types (THESIS / INGEST kept descriptive note that projects add their own)\n- Stockforge-specific anti-patterns (LLM generating numbers, single-perspective thesis, recommending owned stocks)\n- DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md pointer (stockforge bootstrap)\n\nPreserved (portable across projects):\n- Karpathy 4 principles\n- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) — distilled into a 3-row table\n- Session Protocol (Start + End)\n- Memory Tiering (Tier 1 / 2 / 3)\n- Q&A Escalation Doctrine (NO Silent Default)\n- Constitution table (10 portable harness files; explicit note \"stockforge-specific in separate file\")\n- General Hard Rules (domain layer / cross-BC / VBW / no commit / user-prompt-overrides / context-thresholds / tracking retention / ritual demotion)\n- Dispatch Rules + UP-05 skill-tool gating\n- Session Types (PLAN / FOCUSED / MULTI-TASK / VERIFY / RECOVERY / POST-MORTEM only — drop THESIS/INGEST as project-specific)\n- Quality Gates (Tier 1 / 2 / 3)\n- Common Anti-Patterns (general subset only)\n- Layer Manifest pointer\n- Key References (general)\n- \"First Interaction\" guidance (`/session-start`)\n- Project-specific section placeholder (post-/attach population)\n\n### HH-G.3 — Smoke runner design\n\nPer UP-05 doctrine (\"Skill calls only in SUPERVISED mode; gate autonomous loops to NOT call skills\"), the smoke\nrunner does NOT invoke /attach. Instead it deterministically validates the same boundaries /attach would\nenforce, via three checks:\n\n**Check 1: MANIFEST layer-separation** — runs `python -c \"...\"` harness mirroring SKILL.md A1-A7 + 4 new\nassertions HH-G.1 (template existence + token budget + freedom from stockforge identifiers + structural\ncontent). Plus B1-B3 (default_excludes coverage; harness hooks count). Total 14 manifest-level assertions.\n\n**Check 2: STRUCTURAL smoke** — emulates /attach's cp loop against `mktemp -d` target. Copies a\nrepresentative subset of include paths (13 files spanning skills + agents + commands + hooks + manifest +\nconstitution + HH-G.1 template). Verifies: (a) all 13 include paths land at target, (b) 7 stockforge\nexclude paths absent at target, (c) HH-G.1 template content intact post-copy, (d) settings.json contains\nSTOCKFORGE_ env vars (sed-replace would happen at /attach time).\n\n**Check 3: DRY-RUN plan counts** — parses manifest's attach.default_includes / default_excludes / hybrid.hooks.\nAsserts include ≥50 (post-REV-3), exclude ≥20, hybrid ≥1 (drift-signals-D1-D9.sh).\n\nTotal: 21 assertions. Real-state run: 21/21 PASS state=GREEN.\n\n### HH-G companion firing-test\n\nPer Phase 3.5 Hard Rule #2 (and T7 retrofit precedent 63/63 PASS at S79), every new hook ships with companion\nfiring-test. Strategy:\n\n| Test | Synthesis | Asserts |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | real project state | smoke emits state=GREEN |\n| 2 | fixture missing HH-G.1 template | smoke detects [FAIL] HH-G.1 |\n| 3 | fixture with manifest leak (invariants-stockforge.md in default_includes) | smoke detects [FAIL] A3 |\n| 4 | ATTACH_SMOKE_TARGET=$custom env override | smoke uses custom target dir |\n| 5 | exit code semantics | RC=0 on GREEN; RC=1 on RED |\n\nTest 5 originally hit ERR-trap-on-rc1 issue (script exited mid-test); fix: replace direct `bash ...` invocation\nwith `RC=0; bash ... || RC=$?` pattern. Post-fix: 7/7 PASS.\n\n### HH-G.4 checklist extension\n\nExtended `.claude/skills/attach/references/procedures.md` with HH-G.4 portability validation checklist:\n- Pre-flight (5 steps including VBW + smoke + firing-test verification)\n- During /attach (8 verification points)\n- Post-/attach validation (6 target-side checks)\n- Known-issues to suppress (3 items: hybrid hook stubs, personal layer empty, needs-refactor skills)\n- Re-validation triggers (4 trigger conditions)\n\n## Decision\n\nShip 4 artifacts closing Phase 2.5 HH-G:\n\n1. `templates/general-harness/CLAUDE.md` (NEW; 207 LOC; ~2713 tokens) — HH-G.1\n2. `scripts/hooks/attach-portability-smoke.sh` (NEW; ~280 LOC) — HH-G.3 runner\n3. `scripts/hooks/firing-tests/attach-portability-smoke-fire-test.sh` (NEW; ~210 LOC) — companion firing-test\n4. `.claude/skills/attach/references/procedures.md` (EDIT; close to 2.5K target — markdown overhead acceptable)\n- Smoke runner is NOT wired in `.claude/settings.json` chains (manual invocation; manifest changes are episodic, not per-prompt)\n\n### What this does NOT change\n\n- StockForge biz layer (5 stockforge skills + 5 stockforge hooks + project-CLAUDE.md + charter) — untouched\n- /attach skill execution path — skill still works the same; smoke is complementary verification\n- Phase 3.5 T8 charter cool-down — still active until ≥2026-05-09\n- Phase 3.5 T5 protocol mv→constitution (M-S173-1 deny-lift gap) — untouched; orthogonal\n\n## Why (Reasons)\n\n1. **Q4=A user-pick discharge**: S173 user explicitly sequenced HH-G as PRIORITY 1 for S174. This decision = the empirical execution of that pick.\n2. **Phase 2.5 HH-G residue**: 22 sessions S148-S170 silently advanced past HH-G; S172 audit surfaced 3/4 NOT-STARTED. Q-B2 doctrine + verify_phase_before_next_phase doctrine both demand explicit closure not silent skip.\n3. **Phase 3.5 firing-test discipline**: T7 retrofit drained 15→0 backlog at S79. NEW hooks must continue the discipline. This S174 ships smoke runner WITH companion firing-test from day-1.\n4. **UP-05 autonomous-mode skill-tool gating**: smoke runner uses Bash + Python only; no Skill prompts. Aligns with autonomous-protocol Mode-A/D requirements.\n5. **harness-priority-one user doctrine**: harness/system improvement always > product work. User picked A (Recommended): HH-G portability close FIRST. This S174 turn executes that pick.\n\n## Analysis\n\n### HH-G.1 — Template authoring\n\nThe existing `.claude/skills/attach/references/skeleton-templates.md § CLAUDE.md` had a heredoc CLAUDE.md template embedded in skill reference content. That serves /attach's runtime copy mechanism (extract heredoc + write at target). But the Phase 2.5 plan + S172 audit explicitly required a STANDALONE `templates/general-harness/CLAUDE.md` artifact — to live next to other portable templates and be directly inspectable / copyable by ports without going through the skill machinery.\n\nAuthored 207 LOC / ~2713 tokens template stripped of:\n- StockForge VN-stock invariants (NO LLM math, citations, position sizing, bear case, framing rules)\n- Stockforge constitution table entries (`invariants.md` stock-specific, `financial-data-protocol.md`)\n- Stockforge-specific session types (THESIS / INGEST kept descriptive note that projects add their own)\n- Stockforge-specific anti-patterns (LLM generating numbers, single-perspective thesis, recommending owned stocks)\n- DAY_1_CHECKLIST.md pointer (stockforge bootstrap)\n\nPreserved (portable across projects):\n- Karpathy 4 principles\n- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) — distilled into a 3-row table\n- Session Protocol (Start + End)\n- Memory Tiering (Tier 1 / 2 / 3)\n- Q&A Escalation Doctrine (NO Silent Default)\n- Constitution table (10 portable harness files; explicit note \"stockforge-specific in separate file\")\n- General Hard Rules (domain layer / cross-BC / VBW / no commit / user-prompt-overrides / context-thresholds / tracking retention / ritual demotion)\n- Dispatch Rules + UP-05 skill-tool gating\n- Session Types (PLAN / FOCUSED / MULTI-TASK / VERIFY / RECOVERY / POST-MORTEM only — drop THESIS/INGEST as project-specific)\n- Quality Gates (Tier 1 / 2 / 3)\n- Common Anti-Patterns (general subset only)\n- Layer Manifest pointer\n- Key References (general)\n- \"First Interaction\" guidance (`/session-start`)\n- Project-specific section placeholder (post-/attach population)\n\n### HH-G.3 — Smoke runner design\n\nPer UP-05 doctrine (\"Skill calls only in SUPERVISED mode; gate autonomous loops to NOT call skills\"), the smoke\nrunner does NOT invoke /attach. Instead it deterministically validates the same boundaries /attach would\nenforce, via three checks:\n\n**Check 1: MANIFEST layer-separation** — runs `python -c \"...\"` harness mirroring SKILL.md A1-A7 + 4 new\nassertions HH-G.1 (template existence + token budget + freedom from stockforge identifiers + structural\ncontent). Plus B1-B3 (default_excludes coverage; harness hooks count). Total 14 manifest-level assertions.\n\n**Check 2: STRUCTURAL smoke** — emulates /attach's cp loop against `mktemp -d` target. Copies a\nrepresentative subset of include paths (13 files spanning skills + agents + commands + hooks + manifest +\nconstitution + HH-G.1 template). Verifies: (a) all 13 include paths land at target, (b) 7 stockforge\nexclude paths absent at target, (c) HH-G.1 template content intact post-copy, (d) settings.json contains\nSTOCKFORGE_ env vars (sed-replace would happen at /attach time).\n\n**Check 3: DRY-RUN plan counts** — parses manifest's attach.default_includes / default_excludes / hybrid.hooks.\nAsserts include ≥50 (post-REV-3), exclude ≥20, hybrid ≥1 (drift-signals-D1-D9.sh).\n\nTotal: 21 assertions. Real-state run: 21/21 PASS state=GREEN.\n\n### HH-G companion firing-test\n\nPer Phase 3.5 Hard Rule #2 (and T7 retrofit precedent 63/63 PASS at S79), every new hook ships with companion\nfiring-test. Strategy:\n\n| Test | Synthesis | Asserts |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | real project state | smoke emits state=GREEN |\n| 2 | fixture missing HH-G.1 template | smoke detects [FAIL] HH-G.1 |\n| 3 | fixture with manifest leak (invariants-stockforge.md in default_includes) | smoke detects [FAIL] A3 |\n| 4 | ATTACH_SMOKE_TARGET=$custom env override | smoke uses custom target dir |\n| 5 | exit code semantics | RC=0 on GREEN; RC=1 on RED |\n\nTest 5 originally hit ERR-trap-on-rc1 issue (script exited mid-test); fix: replace direct `bash ...` invocation\nwith `RC=0; bash ... || RC=$?` pattern. Post-fix: 7/7 PASS.\n\n### HH-G.4 checklist extension\n\nExtended `.claude/skills/attach/references/procedures.md` with HH-G.4 portability validation checklist:\n- Pre-flight (5 steps including VBW + smoke + firing-test verification)\n- During /attach (8 verification points)\n- Post-/attach validation (6 target-side checks)\n- Known-issues to suppress (3 items: hybrid hook stubs, personal layer empty, needs-refactor skills)\n- Re-validation triggers (4 trigger conditions)\n\n## Decision\n\nShip 4 artifacts closing Phase 2.5 HH-G:\n\n1. `templates/general-harness/CLAUDE.md` (NEW; 207 LOC; ~2713 tokens) — HH-G.1\n2. `scripts/hooks/attach-portability-smoke.sh` (NEW; ~280 LOC) — HH-G.3 runner\n3. `scripts/hooks/firing-tests/attach-portability-smoke-fire-test.sh` (NEW; ~210 LOC) — companion firing-test\n4. `.claude/skills/attach/references/procedures.md` (EDIT; +60 LOC HH-G.4 section) — checklist\n\n### What this means concretely\n\n- Future /attach invocations have a deterministic pre-flight smoke + post-/attach verification path\n- Manifest changes auto-trigger smoke re-validation (per HH-G.4 § Re-validation triggers)\n- Phase 2.5 HH-G residue closed — Phase 3.5 IN-PROGRESS-PARTIAL-S173 status updated to include HH-G done in S174\n- Token budget for portable CLAUDE.md ~2.7K (under 3K cap; Direct invocation triggered ERR trap (set via `trap 'cleanup; exit $RC' ERR EXIT`) → premature script exit mid-test. Output cut off after first PASS line of Test 5; Summary never printed.\n\n**Rule**: When a firing-test deliberately invokes a script expected to return non-zero (testing RED-state detection), use `RC=0; cmd || RC=$?` instead of `cmd; rc=$?`. The `|| RC=$?` form prevents ERR trap firing on the deliberate rc=1.\n\n**Why**: `set -uo pipefail` (without `-e`) does not by itself cause script exit on simple-command failure, BUT `trap '...' ERR EXIT` fires the trap on every non-zero exit of any simple command — and our trap calls `exit $RC` which terminates the script.\n\n**Anti-example**:\n```bash\nbash \"$SMOKE\" >/dev/null 2>&1   # rc=1 → ERR trap → cleanup → exit 1 (mid-test!)\nLEAK_RC=$?                       # never reached\n```\n\n**Correct example**:\n```bash\nLEAK_RC=0\nbash \"$SMOKE\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || LEAK_RC=$?   # rc=1 absorbed by ||; trap not fired\n```\n\n**Severity**: medium. **Auto-detect**: yes (grep firing-tests for `bash.*>.*2>&1$` not preceded by `|| RC=` and followed by `\\$\\?` — candidate hook `firing-test-rc-pattern-lint.sh`; promote-rule cycle catches).\n\n## Mistakes NEW (S174)\n\nNONE — the 2 mid-dev path-conversion + ERR-trap issues were caught during smoke iteration + fixed before any production firing or commit. Output cut off after first PASS line of Test 5; Summary never printed.\n\n**Rule**: When a firing-test deliberately invokes a script expected to return non-zero (testing RED-state detection), use `RC=0; cmd || RC=$?` instead of `cmd; rc=$?`. ERR EXIT` fires the trap on every non-zero exit of any simple command — and our trap calls `exit $RC` which terminates the script.\n\n**Anti-example**:\n```bash\nbash \"$SMOKE\" >/dev/null 2>&1   # rc=1 → ERR trap → cleanup → exit 1 (mid-test!)\nLEAK_RC=$?                       # never reached\n```\n\n**Correct example**:\n```bash\nLEAK_RC=0\nbash \"$SMOKE\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || LEAK_RC=$?   # rc=1 absorbed by ||; trap not fired\n```\n\n**Severity**: medium. **Auto-detect**: yes (grep firing-tests for `bash.*>.*2>&1$` not preceded by `|| RC=` and followed by `\\$\\?` — candidate hook `firing-test-rc-pattern-lint.sh`; promote-rule cycle catches).\n\n## Mistakes NEW (S174)\n\nNONE — the 2 mid-dev path-conversion + ERR-trap issues were caught during smoke iteration + fixed before any production firing or commit.
